pagina.uitlegGebruiker: The tour shows you around in a few steps: where to convert a quotation from the configurator, what happens to your document and what you get back.
pagina.uitlegAdmin: You are an administrator, so after the conversion your tour also covers the server status, the conversion log and the image library. A colleague without administrator rights only sees the first part.

kaart.intro: The tour explains step by step what you see on this screen and where to go. You do not have to fill anything in and nothing changes: it only points things out and explains them — no document is converted along the way. Press Escape to stop, use the arrow keys to page through.
kaart.groepenIntro: Or start right away at the part you need:
kaart.automatisch: Show the tour automatically on a first visit
kaart.automatischUitleg: Stored on this device only and applies to you alone; a colleague logging in here gets their own tour.

welkom.tekst: This app turns a quotation from the configurator into a PDF that is ready for DocuSign. Every checkbox in the document gets an invisible marker, which Salesforce then turns into a tickable DocuSign field. Let me show you how that works in a few steps.

navigatie.tekst: The menu is on the left. Your working screens are at the top; this tour and the language, theme and log-out buttons are at the bottom. On a phone this menu sits at the bottom of the screen, with the less-used items behind the three lines.

serverstatus.titel: Can the server convert right now?
serverstatus.tekst: You see this card as an administrator; your colleagues do not. It tells you before you upload whether the render engine is running and which fonts the server has. If DaxPro is listed as missing here, you still get a PDF, but with a substitute font — and the customer will notice. A red message here means converting will not work at the moment; that is a server problem, not something about your document.

upload.tekst: Drag the .docx file from the configurator in here, or click to browse for it. Only .docx, and no larger than the size shown below the field. Your document is not kept on the server: it is converted and then cleaned up straight away.

starten.tekst: This button sends your document on its way. The server first turns every checkbox into a real character, then renders a PDF and places an invisible marker next to each box in the text layer. That takes a few seconds — give a quotation of dozens of pages a moment.

resultaat.tekst: As soon as it is finished the download starts by itself and a result panel appears below the form. It shows how many checkboxes were found — do check that number, because zero boxes means there is nothing to tick in Salesforce either — how long it took, and whether any font was substituted. The button underneath downloads the PDF again.

geschiedenis.tekst: This lists every conversion anyone has run: who, when, which file, how many boxes and whether it succeeded. Failed attempts are here too, with their error code — useful when a colleague reports that something did not work. Only these details are kept; never the documents themselves. You see this tab as an administrator; your colleagues do not.

beeldbank.tekst: Quotes link the truck photos to the E drive, which the server cannot reach. That is why a copy of the AFBEELDINGEN CPQ folder lives here. Put the whole folder in once; for a new product, upload only the new photos. Whatever is missing here, the app asks the user for while converting. This tab, too, is only visible to you as an administrator.

feedbackGeven.tekst: There is a narrow Support label on the right-hand side of the screen. Click it to send a report with a screenshot attached, and even draw a box around the part you mean. On a phone, Support sits in the menu behind the three lines. It works the same way in every Motrac application.

slot.tekst: You can always come back here: via Guided tour at the bottom of the menu — on a phone behind the three lines. You can take it again, start at one particular part, or switch off the automatic start on a first visit.
